To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the inward current does not need to be voltage-dependent in order to generate oscillations, (2) the inward current needs to be linear in the biological range and (3) the inward current must be balanced by a voltage-gated outward current.

a linear current that has negative conductance in the biological voltage-range is sufficient for producing oscillatory activity, and that such currents can be found in neurons from the stomatogastricsystem.
a regenerative inward ionic current is not necessary to generate neuronal oscillatory activity.

the question of how the properties of the currents in a neuron determine the oscillatory activity of the neuron.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a regenerative inward ionic current is not necessary to generate slow wave oscillations in neurons.
a regenerative inward linear current is sufficient to generate oscillatory activity in a model neuron.
the voltage dependence is not necessary for the inward current to generate oscillations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a linear current that has a negative conductance can play the role of a regenerative, inward current in the generation of oscillations.

a linear current with negative conductance can generate oscillatory behavior, but that the stability of oscillations depends on the precise relationships between the inward, outward and hyperpolarization currents.
the voltage dependence is not necessary for the inward current to be regenerative and for the generation of oscillatory activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
oscillations can emerge from linear and voltage-dependent currents, as long as the conductances of the inward and outward currents are appropriately balanced.
a linear inward current can play the role of a regenerative current, and thus that the voltage-dependent nature of regenerative currents is not necessary for the generation of oscillations.
the oscillations observed in biological neurons can be generated by a simple combination of a regenerative linear current and a non-inactivating voltage-gated outward current.
